display.purpose: Hero-level headlines and primary section titles. One per viewport — never stacked.

headline.purpose: Section openers, card titles in feature contexts.

title.purpose: Sub-section headers, service card titles, form headings.

body.purpose: All running copy. Hard cap at 70ch line length.

label.purpose: Button text, nav links, meta labels. Never lowercase for interactive elements.

shadows.name: ambient-low
shadows.purpose: Smallest-scale surfaces; barely perceptible separation from background.

shadows.name: ambient-mid
shadows.purpose: Default resting state for .card and button active states.

motion.name: ease-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: icon swaps, small opacity changes.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default CSS state transitions: hover backgrounds, border shifts.

motion.name: editorial
motion.purpose: ActionLink arrow badge — intentionally slow for editorial weight.

motion.name: gsap-menu-open

motion.name: gsap-hero-zoom

narrative.overview:
Movara serves leaders who carry real weight: the kind who are scanning the horizon for the shift they know is coming, preparing for disruption before it arrives. This design system reflects that posture. It is warm but never casual, editorial but never decorative. Every surface earns its presence — nothing performs, everything informs.

The palette is grounded in two deliberate anchors: a teal that reads as action and clarity (Horizon Teal), and an amber that reads as hard-won insight (Savanna Gold). Backgrounds stay quiet so content commands. Motion is purposeful — the GSAP-driven menu wipe and hero scroll zoom are moments of intention, not entertainment.

The system explicitly rejects the SaaS-landing-page playbook: no hero metrics, no gradient text, no glass cards, no identical icon-grid service layouts. It also rejects generic African brand visual clichés. This is a consulting firm for boards and leadership teams.
keyCharacteristics: Serif headlines anchored in Hedvig Letters Serif — authoritative without being stiff
Teal as the action signal; amber as the warmth accent; used at different frequencies
Ambient shadows on all resting cards; lift amplifies on hover
GSAP animation for theatrical moments (menu, hero zoom); CSS transitions only for state changes
Body copy capped at 70ch; generous vertical rhythm; no uniform section padding

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Horizon Teal signals action (do this, go here, open this). Savanna Gold signals confirmation and warmth (focused, selected, complete). They must never occupy the same interactive element simultaneously.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Savanna Gold is forbidden as a background color for any element larger than a focus ring or a 2px outline. Its scarcity is what gives it authority.

rules.name: The One-Display Rule
rules.body: A single Display-scale element per viewport height. Multiple display headlines on one screen collapse the hierarchy and dilute authority.

rules.name: The 70ch Ceiling
rules.body: Body copy containers are capped at 70ch width. Layout containers may be wider; text columns are not.

rules.name: The Ambient Floor Rule
rules.body: No interactive card surface is ever shadowless at rest. A card without a shadow is a static decoration. A card with an ambient shadow is an invitation to interact.

rules.name: The Flat-Transition Rule
rules.body: Shadows transition with CSS transition-shadow; transforms translate separately. Never animate both simultaneously on the same property cascade.

dos: Do use Horizon Teal (#38b2ac) as the single action signal — on buttons, links with badges, open menu state, and focus indicators.
Do apply an ambient shadow (shadow-md) to every resting interactive card.
Do cap all body copy containers at 70ch.
Do let the serif headline (Hedvig) carry section authority — one Display-scale headline per viewport, set at weight 400.
Do use Savanna Gold exclusively for focus rings, secondary borders, and hover text accents.
Do use GSAP for theatrical transitions (menu wipe, hero scroll zoom). Use CSS transition for all state changes.
Do use ease-out (power2.out or equivalent) for entrances. Exits use ease-in. Never bounce, never elastic.
Do let section padding vary. The rhythm comes from inconsistency at the macro scale.
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, callouts, or list items.
Don't use glassmorphism. No backdrop-filter: blur on decorative cards.
Don't build the hero-metric template: big number, small label, gradient accent.
Don't render identical icon-grid cards across a service or features section.
Don't use Arizonia (the script logo font) anywhere in body, UI, or marketing copy.
Don't apply Savanna Gold as a fill background on any element larger than a 2px focus ring or border.
Don't use Sky Wash (#DBEAFE) as an error state indicator.
Don't use #000000 or #ffffff as direct values in CSS.
